trickyParts: A9's protocol decides its own answer. Run as three base rounds and then three head rounds on one database, it read POST /asks at +1013% and PATCH /issues/{key} at +10 to +17%; neither was the change. Both databases must be separate copies of one seed, the base at main's schema and the head at this one, and the order must be reversed in every other round, because whichever side runs second is measured while the server is still absorbing the other's 250 writes.

A measurement Postgres that is a Job takes fsync, full_page_writes and synchronous_commit from its manifest's command line, and alter system with a reload cannot move them. Durability off is conservative for A9's relative bound but not what the plan asks for, so the run that counts is on a Job that has them on; synchronous_commit can be turned off for the seed alone with alter database, which is what makes the seed an hour rather than three.

A pod of this deployment reaches a Job in the builds namespace only while that Job's pod template carries the label builds.theorem.dev/reachable: "true". Without it the Job starts, costs its quota and answers nothing, and every connection times out rather than being refused (docs/kubernetes.md, 'Running a workload in the cluster from a role', names this as the one rule admission does not check). mirror.gcr.io/library/postgres carries no pgvector, so the measurement image is mirror.gcr.io/pgvector/pgvector.

A plan assertion decides nothing on a fixture too small for the planner's choice to be real. The probe's document arm read document_search's primary key rather than its GIN index on a 400-document fixture whatever the statement said, and the CTE form passed that assertion only because a non-constant tsquery leaves the planner no estimate - the same ignorance that made it read every project's documents on the measurement database.
deviations: The ten migrations are named for the moment they were created, 20261101182419 to 20261101182522, not renumbered 0158-0167 as the review asked: while this round ran, main took 0158 to 0161 for four migrations of its own and #2633 closed Dispatch's numbered series at 0161, so packages/envoy/migrationid refuses any further number.

ce-simplify-code had never been run on this pull request, which its body recorded as 'not yet run'. It is run now, in the round answering the review rather than the first implementing round, because that is the only slot left before the reviewer reads the head; three findings applied, no statement text, row set, plan or index changed.
openQuestions: R2's share-of-plan reading is recorded in the pull request and its answer is a reason, not a fix: after the change searchQueryMeaning's time is in the meaning arms' embedding reads, each a primary-key lookup of one 1,536-dimension vector per candidate row. No index is missing and no join replaces a per-candidate key lookup.

The related-item check's five-second allowance is close on a production-shaped database whatever the build: this head answers an ask whose check picks twenty lexemes in about 3 s where main takes about 3.3 s, and a project whose term statistics have grown can push either over. That is main's ground as much as this change's, and nothing here moves the allowance.
discoveredComplexity: The forward merge needed two integration fixes that no test named: main's 20261101144855 re-states graph_edges so a block[] pointer is listed only while block_ref_listed holds, and the arm-based backlink count had to repeat that test or answer a number higher than the rows its list shows; and refs.IndexBlocks gained a pointer argument the seed had to pass.

The probe's regression was invisible to every committed test. Its plan assertion passed, its equality test passed, and its A8 reading at three lexemes was a wash; what showed it was A9 driving the ask route on a production-shaped database, where the check ran out its allowance. The fix is in the statement and the reading that now judges it is a pair on one database.
